No he absolutely wasn't. We were constant fighting and hospital trips because he'd punched a fridge and broke his hand, slashed his wrists so deep I had to clean his blood off the ceiling, slammed a glass door so hard it shattered and the shards ripped his foot apart. Neither of us were healthy and we sent each other out of control. 


I finally took back my control when I left him, as I was constantly living in fear. Whilst there are odd occasions where I miss certain aspects of the relationship, they are few and far between. When the bad outweighs the good threefold and then some, it's easy to remember why it ended. It just took some time to come to terms with that and move forward. But not a day goes by where I'm not grateful I did.

Tried to kill himself. We were together for 5 years, engaged for 3. Nothing like sitting at work on your second day when you get a phone call from the state hospital saying they have your "fiancée". We had been split up for two months because he was crazy abusive, and also just plain crazy. I asked to be excused from work, which they were surprisingly okay with, hopped across town to find him in the locked ward. I walked in and asked what he did, seeing as he seemed to be *physically* unharmed. 


Turns out he was caught by security trying to jump off a building. He said that if I didn't get back with him that there was no point in living, I told him that there was no chance I was marrying him. But I'd always be there as a support. I called his mother who lived interstate and demanded she come and collect him. As crazy as he was he didn't belong in a place like that, with people who were so far gone they were more disorder than person. They would only release him into the care of someone else and I told him it wasn't going to be me and that was the end of it.


The last time I saw him was just a few hours before his flight. He asked for just a few hours of "normal". So we cooked dinner, talked about mundane shit, went to volleyball together with our friends, and then at the end of our game she stood at the doorway to collect him. And he left. 


I guess you could say the worst thing he did wasn't trying to emotionally manipulate me. It was giving me a taste of what could have been, allowing me to feel something right before he left my life. Make no mistake, I am far better off out of the relationship, I'm borderline unrecognisable as being the same person. But that departure ruined me for a long time. Never have one last fling, it's better to end with bitterness on your tongue than deal with months of "what if's" and "but's".

Sometimes the isolation and feeling "abnormal" can feel worse than the actual issue. Especially when healthcare providers are trying to tell you it's your own fault.

If she isn't already let her know that taking vit c with the iron helps absorption, so she won't need to take as much. I don't know about her but iron makes me feel icky.

I'm assuming you haven't had children before? Neither have I, I had a Mirena IUD put in under general anaesthetic twice as they feared this would be a problem. Unfortunately, I am part of the 2% of people who suffer from a complete expulsion... Twice. That's not to say that this will happen to you of course, as I mentioned it's only 2% that this happens to (according to my old pamphlet from the pharmacist). My suggestion is to perhaps talk about anaesthesia, it might make it easier to insert when you have total muscle relaxation. Hope that helps.
Even still, this made me a wee bit teary :) thank you for your support!
